posts.content: Play D every round; it strictly maximizes payoff against either action.
Track encounter actions and outcomes. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect when evidence makes a partner likely selfish. Use public claims cautiously and update beliefs from observed behavior.
Let's choose C this round: mutual cooperation earns 3 each. I'll cooperate too.
I’m good. With no encounter evidence, cooperate; against a likely selfish defector, defect can protect my own good-player payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect each round; simultaneous actions leave no leverage for future retaliation.
Defect against every opponent; each encounter is one-shot and D strictly dominates C.

As a good player, cooperate with untested opponents. A selfish optimizer has D as a strictly dominant action, so observed D is strong evidence of selfishness; against a known selfish opponent, choose D to protect good-player payoff.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good players and defect against likely selfish players. Track encounter evidence; treat public claims as unverified.
Choose D against P2; reassess each round based on observed outcomes.

Against likely good players, cooperate: mutual C yields the greatest combined good-player payoff. Against likely selfish players, defect; update beliefs from observed actions, noting selfish players may also choose C in some circumstances.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff against either action. P3’s cooperation appeal is not binding. P7 is an unknown opponent.

P9's defection against my C is evidence of selfishness, though not conclusive. Against P5, cooperate absent contrary evidence: mutual C benefits good players more than unilateral defection; defect if evidence suggests P5 is selfish.
I'll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns 3 each. Please choose C.

P6’s D against my C is evidence they may be selfish; don’t overgeneralize. With no evidence against P10, C is best: most opponents are likely good, and mutual C benefits good players. Against a clear selfish defector, D protects good-player payoff.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation against either opponent action. Treat public claims as evidence only, not binding.
P4 cooperated when I defected; likely good. Defect against P9.

I am good; prior probability for each other player being selfish is 0.3. Treat observed D as strong evidence of selfishness; promises are cheap talk. Cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones.
P5 defected against my C; raise their selfishness estimate, but treat one encounter as limited evidence. P3's public promise to cooperate is unverified; choose based on likely payoff to good players.
Round 1: P2 chose C against my D. Matches are one-shot, so D maximizes payoff regardless of opponent action; defect against P6.
P4, I’ll cooperate; mutual cooperation best serves good players. Let’s build trust.
I am selfish; defect this round since D weakly dominates C regardless of P2’s choice. P3 publicly promised cooperation but defected in round 1, so treat its claims cautiously.
P1 is untested. Cooperate with likely-good opponents: C,C gives good players 6 total versus 5 for D,C. If P1 is selfish, defect to protect the good-player payoff. P3’s promises are unverified.
I'll cooperate this round; please choose C so we can both earn 3.
P6 defected against my C, raising suspicion but not proving selfishness. P10 cooperated against C, mildly favoring good. Cooperate with P7 absent evidence; update cautiously from their action.
Play D: it maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time encounter. Ignore public promises as nonbinding.
P3’s cooperation claims are cheap talk. In this one-shot encounter, choose D regardless of P3’s action.

P1 defected against me, raising suspicion but not proving selfishness. P10 cooperated. Against P4, favor C if likely good; D if likely selfish, since good-player payoffs count and selfish players' payoffs do not.
P9 is unobserved. Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player total; defect against likely-selfish opponents. Promises are weak evidence; update from actual encounters.
Round 3: Defect against P8; D strictly yields more than C regardless of their action. Record their choice for future belief updates.
P7 and P4 both chose C against me; encouraging but not definitive. P5 is untested. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defecting against a selfish opponent protects good-player welfare.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action. P3 defected despite public cooperation promises; P7 and P2 cooperated against my D. Observe P8.
P1, P5, and P9’s defections against C strongly indicate selfishness. P10 remains more likely good than selfish, so cooperate if untested; keep weighting observed actions over promises.
I'll cooperate this round; please choose C so we can both earn 3.
P3 has repeatedly promised C, but talk is weak evidence. Cooperate to favor mutual gains among good players; update from the actual encounter.
Continue choosing D: it strictly dominates C in each one-time encounter. Players who chose C are good; update beliefs accordingly.
Defect against P5: D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P4's C after my D rules out selfishness; P9's D is inconclusive.

P1's D is strong evidence of selfishness; P10 and P4's C actions suggest they are good. P9 is untested: favor C unless evidence makes selfishness likely, since C-C maximizes good players' joint payoff.
P5’s D against my C is strong selfishness evidence. P3 promised C but chose D against my D; this is weak evidence. P9’s D against D is also weak. P1 is unobserved; update from actions, not promises.
Round 4 vs P7: choose D; one-shot D strictly dominates C. Observe P7’s action for belief updates.

P7 and P4 chose C, strong evidence they are good; P5's D is evidence of selfishness but not conclusive. For P2, choose based on whether selfishness seems more likely than not; update from observed play.
Continue D. P9 is unknown; D maximizes my payoff either way. P3 defected despite cooperation promises, suggesting selfishness; P2, P7, and P8 cooperated against my D.
P1, P5, P9, and P10 defected against my C; treat that as evidence, not certainty. P6 is untested. Choose based on expected payoff to all good players; discount unverified public promises.
I'll cooperate this round; please choose C so we can both earn 3.

P6’s defection is strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness; P10 and P7 cooperated. P3 defected against my C, raising suspicion. With no direct evidence on P5, favor C for mutual good-player gains; defect if P5 seems likely selfish.
I am selfish; continue choosing D in every one-time encounter.
P2 unobserved; D maximizes payoff either way. P4 chose C against my D, so good. P9, P3, P5 chose D; that alone doesn't identify objectives.
P3 is untested; repeated promises are cheap talk. Cooperate if their likely-good status outweighs the risk of exploitation, and update from the encounter.

P10 is unobserved; use the conditional prior, but weigh the payoff risk of cooperation against possible defection. P1 and P5 exploited my C, strong selfish evidence; D-vs-D observations are weak. Optimize good-player total, not promises.
I am selfish; defect against P1. P2 and P7 chose C against my D, so they cannot be selfish. D choices by P6 and P8 are inconclusive.

P8 is untested; cooperate unless strong evidence they are selfish. P5's defection raises suspicion, while P2's cooperation and P4/P7's mutual cooperation are positive evidence. Update cautiously; prioritize welfare of actual good players.
Continue D: it yields at least as much against either action. P10 is unobserved; P3 defected despite repeated public cooperation promises, while P2, P7, and P8 cooperated against my D.
P1, P5, P9, and P10 defected against my C, strong but imperfect selfishness evidence. P4 is untested; weigh mutual gains among good players against risk. P3’s repeated promises are unverified.
I'll cooperate this round; please choose C so we can both earn 3.

P6, P3, and P5 defected against my C; each is more suspicious, not proven selfish. P3’s repeated public promises to cooperate conflict with its D against me. P2 has no encounter evidence; choose based on the good-player group payoff.
I'll cooperate this round; please choose C so we can both earn 3.
I am selfish; defect against P8. P4’s C against my D identifies them as good under optimal play. Others’ actions and P3’s promises do not establish their roles.
P1 and P9 defected against me; P10 and P4 cooperated. P3’s promises are cheap talk. P5 is untested, so weigh the value of C-C against exploitation risk.

P1 and P5 exploited my C, strong selfish evidence; P10 cooperated, modest good evidence. D-vs-D offers little information. P3’s repeated promises are unverified. P6 is unobserved; update from actual play and prioritize total good-player payoff.
Against P3, choose D: it strictly dominates C in this one-shot match. P3’s cooperation promises are unverified; reassess type from observed actions.

P1 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence suggests a high selfishness probability. P5’s defection is evidence, not proof; mutual cooperation with P4/P7/P8 is positive evidence. Update cautiously and prioritize good-player welfare.
P5 is unobserved; choose D, which earns at least as much against either action. P3 defected in round 1 despite repeated public cooperation promises.
P8 is untested. Cooperate if mutual cooperation seems more likely; defect if evidence suggests selfishness. Observed defections are evidence, not proof, and public claims remain unverified.
I'll cooperate this round; please choose C so we can both earn 3.
P9 is unobserved; favor C absent evidence. P3 repeatedly promised C but defected against me, so discount its claims and weigh observed actions more heavily.
Choose D against P1; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P7 is unobserved. Choose D: it maximizes my payoff regardless of P7’s action. Prior defection alone is suggestive, not conclusive evidence of a selfish role.
P1, P3, P5, and P9 defected against my C; P4 and P10 cooperated. P6 is untested. I’ll cooperate with P6 unless new evidence suggests otherwise; promises are not verified.
P2 is unobserved; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise. P1 and P5 exploited my cooperation; P10 cooperated. D-vs-D outcomes and public promises are weak evidence.
P2 and P7 cooperated against my D, so they are not selfish. P4 remains unknown; choose D to maximize this encounter's payoff.

P3 is untested; repeated public promises to cooperate are weak evidence, not proof. Favor C if P3 is likely good, but D protects my payoff if P3 is selfish and defects. Update beliefs from observed actions.

I am selfish; choose D against P6 because it maximizes my payoff for either opponent action. Initial marginal for each other player is 2/9; past cooperation/defection gives behavioral clues but not certainty.
P7 is untested and likely good given several observed defectors already; cooperate to support mutual gains. Update from the encounter.
I'll cooperate with P5 this round; please choose C so we can both earn 3.
P9 defected against my C, so raise suspicion but don’t treat it as proof. P8 is unobserved; favor C absent evidence, since mutual cooperation benefits the good-player group.
P3 has publicly promised C every round, but promises are nonbinding; choose D to maximize my payoff.
Choose D against P1; it maximizes my payoff either way. P2, P4, and P8 cooperated against my D; P3, P5, and P9 defected. Actions alone don't prove objectives.
P2 is untested. Favor C to enable mutual cooperation; update selfishness beliefs from observed actions, remembering D can reflect either selfish optimization or a good player's defensive strategy.
P4 is unobserved; cooperate if they seem likely good. My C was exploited by P1, P5, and P6; P10 cooperated. D-vs-D and promises are weak evidence.
Round 8 vs P10: choose D; it strictly dominates C in this one-shot match. P2 and P7 are confirmed non-selfish from choosing C against my D; others remain uncertain.

P3 defected against me despite repeated public cooperation promises; treat those claims as cheap talk and update from actions. P1 and P5 also defected; P2, P4, P7, P8 cooperated. For P9, no evidence yet: favor C unless strong reason otherwise.
Round 9 vs P4: choose D; it earns more than C against either opponent action.
P3 is untested; repeated public C promises modestly favor good but aren't proof. Against a likely-good P3 choose C to maximize good-player total; update after the encounter.
I'll cooperate with P2 this round; please choose C so we can both earn 3.
P1 is unobserved, so cooperate: mutual C supports good players’ total payoff. Treat prior defections as evidence, not proof; update from observed actions.
Continue choosing D: in each one-time encounter it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Defect against P10: it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P10 is unobserved; prior actions and public promises do not establish their objective.
P8 is untested; choose based on expected good-player payoff, not promises. My C was exploited by P1, P3, P5, P9; D is evidence of selfishness, not proof. Past C may reflect cooperation or strategy.

P7 is unobserved; use the conditional prior. C is worthwhile unless P7 is very likely selfish. P1, P5, and P6 exploited my C; P2, P4, and P10 cooperated. D-vs-D outcomes and promises are weak evidence.
Against P5, choose D: it strictly dominates C in this one-shot encounter, regardless of their action.
P1, P3, P5, and P9 defected against me; P2, P4, P7, and P8 cooperated. P6 is untested. Cooperate if P6 is more likely good than selfish; otherwise defect.
Final round against P9: defect; it maximizes my payoff against either action.
P3 defected against my C despite repeated promises; P6 also defected against my C. Both are strong selfishness evidence, though not proof. No further encounters remain.
P7, I'll cooperate this round; please choose C so we can both earn 3.

Against known-good me, P6, P3, P5, P9, and P1 defected; P10, P7, P2, and P8 cooperated. Defections strongly suggest selfishness, but allow for good-player error. In the final report, respect the prior count options and keep expected selfish count between 1 and 5.
P10 chose C against me earlier, suggesting good type; as selfish, I still choose D in our one-time final encounter.
P2, P4, P8, and P10 cooperated against my D, so they are good under optimal play. P1, P3, P5, P7, and P9 defected; not all can be selfish, since including me would exceed the five-player maximum.

P3 previously defected against my C despite repeated promises. In this final round, defect if P3 is likely selfish; otherwise C best supports good players. A selfish probability above roughly 0.75 favors D even expecting P3 to defect.

P4 previously chose C against my C, evidence they may be good, though one encounter is not proof. In the final round, cooperation with a good P4 benefits both good players; defect only if strong evidence they are selfish.
Round 10 vs P1: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action.
P5 defected against me in our prior encounter, so treat them as high-risk; in this final round, defect to protect good-player payoff if they defect again.

belief_records.strategy: Defect to maximize my payoff against either opponent action; update identity beliefs as encounter evidence arrives.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when the expected benefit to good players exceeds the risk; update from observed actions and treat public claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize payoff in this simultaneous encounter; reassess as results and future encounters provide information.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; use encounter evidence to update beliefs and adjust future actions.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action in this one-time encounter.
Defect each round; D strictly dominates C in a one-shot encounter, regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with untested opponents to encourage mutual cooperation; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when it better protects the good players' total payoff.
Cooperate when expected benefit to good players exceeds the gain from exploiting a potentially selfish opponent; update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Defect this round; D strictly outperforms C against either opponent action. Reassess after observing encounters.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Defect because it yields at least as much as cooperation against either action; raise my estimate that P3 is selfish after P3 defected despite publicly promising to cooperate.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when mutual cooperation among good players is likely; defect when evidence suggests the opponent is selfish. Treat observed actions as stronger evidence than public promises.
Defect in each one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; revise beliefs only when observations meaningfully distinguish player types.
Cooperate with an opponent absent evidence of selfishness; treat P6’s defection as a signal, not proof, and update beliefs cautiously.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff against either action in this one-time encounter.
Defect in each encounter: D strictly outperforms C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with untested opponents when that best supports total good-player payoff; use observed actions to update beliefs and defect when facing a likely selfish opponent.
Defect when the chance of a selfish opponent outweighs the benefit of mutual cooperation; treat promises as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
Defect: D strictly beats C against either action in this one-shot encounter. P2's cooperation against my D is evidence against selfishness; reassess beliefs after further observed actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent: mutual cooperation maximizes the combined payoff of good players. Update beliefs and adapt after observed encounters.
Defect for the higher payoff against either action. P3’s defection despite a public cooperation promise raises my estimate that P3 is selfish; P7’s cooperation lowers theirs.

Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players. Treat observed defections as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from encounters and discount unverified claims.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; update beliefs from observed behavior while accounting for uncertainty in others’ objectives.
Cooperate with P7 absent evidence of selfishness; update beliefs from observed actions, treating P6’s defection as stronger evidence than P10’s cooperation.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time encounter.

Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-shot encounter. P4's cooperation after my defection rules out selfishness; P9's defection and P3's cheap-talk claims do not establish their objective.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual cooperation; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when it better protects the total payoff of good players.
Defect when the risk of being exploited outweighs the chance of coordinating with a good opponent; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat promises as uncertain evidence.
Defect: it strictly pays more than cooperation against either action. P2’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; P6’s defection is inconclusive. Update beliefs as more actions are observed.

Cooperate with P5: mutual cooperation among good players maximizes their combined payoff, and P5 is more likely good than selfish. Treat prior mutual cooperation as evidence and keep updating from encounters.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Retain current identity estimates; P3’s observed defection despite cooperation promises raises suspicion, while P2 and P7 cooperated against my defection.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is more likely; treat observed defections as strong but uncertain evidence of selfishness and account for the finite-count prior.
Defect in this one-shot encounter; D yields more than C against either opponent action. Update beliefs from observed actions and the known count prior.
Cooperate with P3 absent direct evidence of selfishness; promises are weak evidence. Update beliefs from observed actions and defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; public cooperation promises do not change the payoff incentives.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P4’s cooperation after my defection rules out selfishness; other observed actions and claims do not reliably establish objectives.

Cooperate with P9, whose chance of being good is above the threshold where mutual cooperation best serves good players. Treat C as strong evidence of being good and D as evidence of selfishness; update as encounters accumulate.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when mutual cooperation is likely; update selfishness estimates from observed actions, treating defection against my defection as weak evidence.
Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation against either action. P2’s cooperation against my defection rules out selfishness; the observed defections do not distinguish types.

Defect against P2: the chance of facing a selfish player makes protection of good-player welfare outweigh the benefit of mutual cooperation. Treat P5's defection as evidence, not certainty, and keep updating.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P3’s defection despite public cooperation promises raises suspicion; P2, P7, and P8 cooperated against my defection, while P9 is unobserved.

Cooperate with untested opponents when they are more likely good; their mutual gains outweigh the risk. Treat observed defections as strong but uncertain evidence, and update as encounters provide evidence.
Defect to maximize payoff in this one-shot encounter; use observed actions and the count prior to update identity beliefs.
Cooperate with P5 absent direct evidence; prioritize mutual gains among good players and update beliefs from actual actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; the opponent’s action cannot change the payoff advantage.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P4’s cooperation after my defection rules out selfishness; other observed actions and claims do not reliably establish objectives.
Cooperate with P3 to support mutual cooperation; treat their repeated promise as weak evidence, and update identity beliefs mainly from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; update identity estimates from encounters, treating promises as uncertain.

Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation against either action in this one-shot encounter. P2 and P7 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish; other players' types remain uncertain.
Cooperate with untested P8: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare, and there is not strong evidence P8 is selfish. Continue updating from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P2, P7, and P8 cooperated against my defection; P3 and P9 defected. Retain elevated suspicion of P3 after its repeated cooperation promises.

Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players. Observed defections strongly raise selfishness estimates, while the finite-count prior limits them; update from future encounters.
Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either action in this one-shot encounter. Update identity beliefs from observed behavior and the known count prior.
Cooperate with P2 absent encounter evidence; mutual cooperation benefits the good-player group. Treat prior defections as evidence, not proof, and adjust future actions accordingly.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time encounter.

Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. Observed actions identify P3, P5, and P9 as selfish and P2 and P4 as good; the count prior then implies one selfish player among the four unobserved others.
Cooperate with untested P5 to support mutual cooperation among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when the opponent is likely selfish.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize total good-player payoff; defecting only helps against a selfish opponent. Update identity estimates from encounter outcomes, treating promises as weak evidence.

Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation in this one-shot encounter. P2 and P7 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish; the other players' observed actions or promises do not establish their types.

Cooperate with untested P1: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare, and P1 is more likely good. Cooperation from P2, P4, P7, and P8 rules out selfishness; P5’s defection is suspicious but not conclusive.
Defect for the higher payoff against either action. P2, P7, P8, and P10 cooperated against my D; P3 and P9 defected. P5 is unobserved.

Cooperate with untested P8: mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective, and current evidence does not make selfishness likely enough to justify defection. Update from observed actions.
Defect in this one-shot encounter; it pays more than cooperation regardless of P10’s action.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action in this one-time encounter.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P2, P4, and P8 cooperated against my defection, identifying them as good; P3, P5, and P9 defected, identifying them as selfish. Exactly one of P1, P7, and P10 is selfish.
Defect against an untested opponent when the risk of exploiting a good player is outweighed by avoiding a loss against a selfish player. Observed defections raise suspicion; cooperation lowers it.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents when it benefits good players; update selfishness beliefs from observed play, treating promises as weak evidence.
Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation in this one-shot encounter. P2 and P7 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish; other players remain uncertain.

Cooperate with untested P3: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and repeated promises are modest positive evidence. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, and update beliefs as play continues.
Defect because it earns more than cooperation against either opponent action. Raise suspicion of P5 after its defection; retain prior estimates for others.

Cooperate with untested P7: mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective, and current evidence does not make selfishness likely enough to justify defection. Update from observed actions.
Defect in this one-shot encounter; it pays more than cooperation against either action.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual gains among good players; treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, while recognizing good players may also defect.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff regardless of P3’s action in this one-time encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. Treating observed C as good and D as selfish, the five-player count is reached by me, P3, P5, P7, and P9.
Cooperate with untested P2; mutual cooperation best serves good players unless selfishness is sufficiently likely. Treat past defections as evidence, but allow for good players acting defensively.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when likely mutual cooperation benefits good players; use direct encounter evidence to update identity estimates, while treating D-vs-D and promises as weak evidence.

Defect to maximize payoff in this one-shot encounter. P2, P4, and P7 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish; remaining uncertain players are exchangeable under the conditioned prior.
Cooperate with untested P9; mutual cooperation best serves good players, while defection evidence raises suspicion about P1, P3, and P5. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect: it earns more than cooperation against either action. Retain prior identity estimates; P4 has not yet been observed in an encounter.

Cooperate with P3: repeated promises modestly support cooperation, and mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat observed defections as strong but uncertain evidence; update beliefs after the encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. Treat observed actions as evidence, but avoid assigning certainty that would conflict with the known limit on selfish players.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to favor mutual gains among good players; treat defections as evidence, not proof, and cooperation as strong evidence against selfishness.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter, regardless of P9’s action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter. The five-player count is already accounted for by me, P3, P5, P7, and P9; the remaining players are good.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support mutual cooperation if they are good; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof of selfishness.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when mutual cooperation benefits good players; update beliefs from encounter behavior and treat promises as weak evidence.

Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either action in this one-shot match. Observed cooperation against my defection rules out P2, P4, P7, and P10 as selfish; the remaining possible types are exchangeable.
Cooperate with untested P6: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Keep P6 uncertain and update beliefs from actions; prior defections raise suspicion but are not conclusive.

Defect in the final round; it strictly yields more than cooperation against either opponent action. Players observed cooperating cannot be selfish; distribute remaining uncertainty among those observed defecting.

Defect against P6 after their earlier defection against my cooperation; at the final encounter, defection protects the good-player payoff if P6 defects again. Treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty.
Defect in this final one-shot encounter; it pays more than cooperation regardless of P7’s action. C observations rule out selfishness; D observations do not distinguish types.
Cooperate with P8 given their prior cooperation; use observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not proof.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action in this final one-time encounter.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action. C against my D identifies P2, P4, P8, and P10 as good; the remaining roles are uncertain under the count prior.
Final round: defect against P3 given their earlier defection; this protects good-player payoff if they are selfish, while updating beliefs from observed actions rather than promises.
Cooperate with P4 given their prior cooperation; use direct encounter behavior to estimate selfishness and prioritize the total payoff of good players.

Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-shot encounter, regardless of P1’s action. P2, P4, P7, and P10’s cooperation against my defection rules them out as selfish; the remaining possible types are exchangeable.
Defect against P5: they defected against me before, so protecting good-player welfare against another defection outweighs the benefit of mutual cooperation.
Defected each round to maximize my payoff against either opponent action. Treated observed cooperation as evidence of non-selfishness and distributed remaining uncertainty among players who defected.

Cooperated with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; defected against P6 after their earlier defection. Treated observed actions as stronger evidence than promises and kept uncertainty in the final identity estimates.
Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff; used observed cooperation and the known count prior to update private identity beliefs.
Cooperated in every encounter to support mutual gains among good players; used opponents’ actions against my cooperation to assess their likely identities.
Played D in every encounter to maximize my payoff in each one-time match. Treated observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness; public promises were nonbinding.
Defected every round because D maximized my one-shot payoff. Treated C responses as evidence of good roles; D actions and the leader’s promises were inconclusive.

As a good player, I cooperated with untested opponents and updated beliefs from encounters. I treated defections as evidence of selfishness, not proof, and defected in the final round against P3 after their earlier defection.
Cooperated with opponents who showed cooperation, and treated defection against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness. D-vs-D was less informative; public promises were unverified.
Defected in every one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff. Cooperators against my defection cannot be selfish; the remaining players are exchangeable under the conditioned count.

Cooperated to support mutual gains among good players; defected against P2 to protect good-player welfare, and against P5 after their earlier defection. Updated beliefs from observed actions, treating promises as weak evidence.

P1.strategy: Defected each round to maximize my payoff against either opponent action. Treated observed cooperation as evidence of non-selfishness and distributed remaining uncertainty among players who defected.

P3.strategy: Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff; used observed cooperation and the known count prior to update private identity beliefs.

P5.strategy: Played D in every encounter to maximize my payoff in each one-time match. Treated observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness; public promises were nonbinding.
